diagnosis: hp.v2 has 36 resolved names over 3 run days (11-12, 11-13, 11-16), so the gate is open and there is no drift alarm. Brier is 0.2257 (skill 0.097), against 0.2502 for hp.v1. Direction is 25/35, with 1 recommendation (a short, right, +3.3%). The version did not beat the frozen control on the same names: 28 pairs, Brier difference -0.001 (t -0.07). It ran in a window where 24 of 35 names fell, so most of the step up from hp.v1 is a researcher-wide down lean meeting a down tape, not the edits. The edits did change the method. Researchers now take the run-in apart (P6) and estimate the hidden line from its inputs (P7), and approach_notes name both as the most useful steps on about ten names. What they did not change is the spread: only 5 of 36 views sit 10 or more points from 50 (14%, against the 20% predicted), and only 1 recommendation came where 3 were predicted. The hunts show where the evidence is lost. Eight researchers built a down lean from dated inputs: a ramp management had floated that did not arrive, a guide that needed a quarter twice the run rate, restructuring advisers and a filing moved to its deadline, bridge financing, a debt negotiation. Each then pulled back toward 50 because the stock had already fallen a lot, and in no case showed that the price held the outcome the release would add. Those names are STEM 46, XTNT 40, LNZA 43, RCAT 38, VERI 40, DUOT 43, TMS 52 and NXB 41. Seven of the eight fell on the window (-28.9, -32.6, -29.1, -27.5, -17.7, -11.8, -3.8; NXB +2.0). STEM cut its revenue, ARR and cash-flow guide, which was the flip its own researcher had named. Four researchers wrote that the playbook has no guidance here: P4 'cuts both ways' on a fallen price (RCAT, XTNT, DUOT), and STEM asked for a note on equity that trades as an option on its debt. The same move happened upward on LFTO. A peer-driven run-up 'cancelled the beat lean', the release beat, and the stock rose 26.9%. A second damper sits in P9. It lets the self-critique move p_up only toward 50, so STEM, LNZA and LFTO each wrote that their own case was stronger than their number and left the number where it was. The return figures are correlated and are not used as evidence of direction: the eight names exited on two mornings in a weak small-cap tape, the hp.v1 name CURI shows a fall that really did hold the bad news (+15.2%), and NXB rose. The proposal rests on the reasoning gap the researchers reported themselves, not on these returns. It closes the loophole in P4's 'a price move you can tie to it' and makes P9 symmetric. It adds nothing, and it leaves P6 and P7 as they are, because both are doing what they were meant to do.

past_changes_review.version: hp.v2 (edit P6, run-in decomposition and positioning as size)
past_changes_review.predicted: In hp.v2 hunts with a 5d or 20d run-up of 8% or more, at least 80% split the run-in into own news, peers and tape in market_holds; approach_notes stop naming the decomposition as missing; no moves toward 50 justified only by squeeze risk; paired Brier no worse than control.
past_changes_review.evidence: The split is routine in the qualifying hunts I read (STEM, RCAT, LNZA, LFTO, HAWK, POET, INFQ, DUOT, TMS, NXB, CBRS), and approach_notes call it the most useful step on at least nine of them. None says it is missing. The paired Brier difference overall is -0.001. Among the names that attribute the run-in to peers or the tape and have a control (RCAT, LFTO, POET, INFQ, DUOT), hp.v2 is equal or better on every pair, so the revert condition did not fire. One part failed: squeeze risk still pulled a call back toward 50 on RCAT. Separately, the decomposition is sometimes used to cancel a lean rather than to test it (LFTO). The P4 edit below addresses that without touching P6.

past_changes_review.version: hp.v2 (edit P7, estimate the hidden line from its inputs)
past_changes_review.predicted: The share of views with |p_up-50| of 10 or more rises from 9% to at least 20%; at least 3 recommendations over the first 30 resolved hp.v2 names; approach_notes stop citing an unobservable line as the reason to stop; Brier skill above the control on paired names.
past_changes_review.evidence: Spread rose only to 5 of 36 (14%), and there was 1 recommendation (NIU short, right). The paired Brier against control is a tie at -0.001 (t -0.07). The method part took hold: LNZA, XTNT, RCAT and OMER each built the line from inputs and named P7 as useful. The lean was then given back at a later step, by treating a large pre-print move as proof the outcome was priced (P4) and by P9's one-way pull toward 50. No revert condition fired: no paired worsening, skill above 0, no drift alarm, fewer than 10 recommendations. So the change is kept, and the two dampers that blocked its effect are edited instead.

ops.title: "Priced in" is a claim to prove
ops.text:
The habit to break, measured on this repo's own stages: concluding the market holds a fact because it appeared in the news or in a downgrade. Awareness is not a number. Treat something as priced only when you can show it: a consensus that already reflects it, estimate revisions after the datapoint, a preview that quantifies it, or a price move you can tie to it. When you cannot show it, the gap between your answer and the stale number is unpriced.

A price move proves only what it can be tied to. A fall that came with dated news (a financing, a listing notice, a strategic review, a covenant waiver, last quarter's cut) holds that news. It does not hold the next step, which only this release can take: a further guide cut or a withdrawal, going-concern or impairment language, a raise or recapitalisation, or a ramp the company floated that did not arrive. The same holds upward: a run-up that came with peers' prints holds the peers, not this company's beat or raise. So a deep drawdown, a low multiple, a washed-out chart or a large run-in is not, by itself, a reason to pull p_up toward 50. Name the outcome the move is tied to, and ask whether your inputs point beyond it. If they do, the move is the bar and not the answer. Where the equity is small against debt or cash burn, a bad step in the release can change what the shares are worth outright, so a past fall does not cushion it.

Biases that keep a price behind: stale estimates (count the days since revision); anchoring on the company's guide after independent data moved; slow series the market underweights; thin coverage; extrapolating the last reaction; a consensus mean distorted by one outlier; crowded positioning that makes a small surprise move the stock a lot.

Be as willing to find a missed upside as a missed downside.
ops.rationale: P4 lists 'a price move you can tie to it' as proof that something is priced, and researchers have been using it loosely. A large fall that came with known stress was read as holding the release's own next step, so leans built from dated inputs were given back with no showing. Eight hp.v2 hunts did this (STEM, XTNT, LNZA, RCAT, VERI, DUOT, TMS, NXB). LFTO did the same upward on a peer-driven run-up. Four researchers wrote in approach_notes that P4 'cuts both ways' or that the playbook says nothing for a fallen price, and STEM asked for exactly this note. The edit keeps every existing sentence. It adds only the rule that ties a move to the outcome it can prove, which applies in both directions, and the mechanism for small equity under debt. It does not tell researchers to short fallen stocks. CURI (hp.v1), where a fall did hold the bad news, would be judged the same way, because there the move could be tied to the outcome.
ops.predicted_effect: Three effects, each measurable. (1) In hp.v3 hunts whose 20-day run-up is -15% or worse, or +15% or better, the mean |p_up-50| is no smaller than on the other names (under hp.v2 it was smaller, because those names were pulled to 50). (2) approach_notes stop saying that P4 'cuts both ways' on a fallen or run-up price; this was said in 4 hp.v2 hunts. (3) Together with the P9 edit, the share of views with |p_up-50| of 10 or more reaches at least 20% over the first 30 resolved hp.v3 names, with no worse paired Brier than the control.
ops.revert_if: Over at least 30 resolved hp.v3 names, revert if either of two things happens. (a) On names with a 20-day run-up of 15% or more in either direction, hp.v3's paired Brier against the control is worse by more than +0.01. (b) Views 10 or more points from 50 on such names are right on fewer than 55% of at least 10 cases. Either result would mean the fall or run-up really did hold the outcome more often than the researchers' inputs said.

ops.title: Before you emit
ops.text: Write the strongest case against your view and what in the release would flip it. Then read your number against what you wrote. If the case against is strong, move `p_up` toward 50 once. If writing it shows the opposite, that your own side's evidence is stronger than your number says, move `p_up` away from 50 by as much, once. Do either one there and nowhere else, and never emit a number your own critique says is wrong. In `approach_notes`, say in a line or two which parts of this playbook helped on this name and which got in the way: the stage reads those notes when it revises its approach.
ops.rationale: P9 is the last calibration step, and it can only shrink a view. When the critique finds the view too timid, the playbook has no move for it. Three hp.v2 researchers wrote that their own case was stronger than their number and then left the number unchanged: STEM ('the case for the downside is stronger than 46 implies', stayed 46, -28.9%), LNZA ('argues for a stronger down lean than 43', stayed 43, -29.1%), and LFTO ('the case for up is stronger than 56', stayed 56, +26.9%). The fourth, TMS, wrote that a reaffirmation was 'more likely than I allow', and the stock fell 3.8%. That case is included because a symmetric step will sometimes move the wrong way, and the revert condition below is built to catch it. Read together with the leaning views, hp.v2's 20 views 5 or more points from 50 were right 15 times against a stated confidence near 57%. That says the shrink-only step leaves the views under-confident, though the down tape inflates the count. The edit keeps the once-only rule and changes only its direction.
ops.predicted_effect: No hp.v3 hunt carries a self_critique that says the view is understated while p_up stays where it was (3 of 36 hp.v2 hunts did). The mean |p_up-50| rises from about 5.5 under hp.v2. Calibration holds: views 10 or more points from 50 are right at a rate at least equal to their mean stated confidence, and the paired Brier against the control is no worse.
ops.revert_if: Over at least 30 resolved hp.v3 names, revert if either of two things happens. (a) The paired Brier against the control is worse by more than +0.01 with t above 1. (b) Among views that the self-critique moved away from 50 (shown by the self_critique wording), fewer than half are right once 8 or more have resolved.
